Subject: Re: PII scrubbing + sampling guidance for VPC SIEM export

Jun —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level answers first, then I attached a short bundle with configs and scrub examples.

Sampling strategy (summary):
- Default: continuous, low-rate sampling for high-volume diagnostics (1/1000 events) to protect throughput and cost.
- Deterministic sampling for error traces and alerts (always keep events with severity >= ERROR).
- Configurable session-based sampling for request traces (customers can set 100% for last-mile debug windows).

PII/PHI scrubbing (summary):
- We apply transform hooks in the forwarder before data leaves the tenant VPC. Typical steps: tokenization of obvious PII (emails, phone numbers), redaction of long numeric strings (suspected SSNs), and optional field-level hashing for identifiers.
- By default we do not retain raw payloads in our export bundles; the forwarder can be configured to strip payloads at the HTTP layer and forward only structured metadata and traces.

Evidence/artifacts: attached is a short PDF (redwood-vpc-scrub-guidelines-v1.pdf) that describes the default pipelines, and a sample forwarder config (redwood-sample-config.yaml) that operators can run in staging to validate.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kimberly and Hiro will provide a compact regex list and checklist (for your compliance rubric) — see follow-up.
2) If Acme needs a signed attestation for the audit we can provide a DocuSign-backed SOC2 evidence bundle (I will include a link or sign request once legal OKs the artifact).

Looping K. and H.

Jun / Dylan —

Adding the checklist and a minimal set of regex patterns we've used in customer on-prem forwarders. These are intended to be applied at the forwarder inbound pipeline (Lua/Go filter) before any batching/export.

Checklist (high level):
- Ensure forwarder runs in the tenant VPC with customer-managed SGs; restrict egress to Redwood endpoints only.
- Enable prefix/KV cache disabled for exported fields that may contain PHI unless explicit allowlist present.
- Turn on ‘redact-mode: strict’ for audit-sensitive workloads; this will replace matched tokens with <<REDACTED>>.
- Keep an export sampling log (hash of removed values) for traceability without storing raw tokens.

Example regex snippets (attach in file pii-redaction-regex.txt):
- email: [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}
- phone (US): (?:\+1[-\.\s]?)?\(?\d{3}\)?[-\.\s]?\d{3}[-\.\s]?\d{4}
- SSN-like: \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b

Caveats and recommendations:
- Avoid in-line regex that processes full request bodies at high volume; prefer structured-field scrubbing or sampling at source to keep costs predictable.
- For PHI datasets we recommend hashing identifiers and forwarding only keyed metrics (counts/aggregates) rather than raw events.

Attachment: pii-redaction-regex.txt (contains the expanded list + caveat notes).

If Acme needs, we can run a short acceptance test (2–4 hours) in a staging forwarder and produce a signed checklist showing the rules triggered and samples redacted.

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
